item.title: Protesters set fire to migrant camp in Ceuta
item.description: The unrest comes one month after a mass influx of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish exclave in North Africa.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Spain: Thieves steal Bronze Age gold in lightning raid on Villena Museum
item.description: One of the world's greatest Bronze Age gold collections has been swiped, almost in its entirety, from Villena Museum. A highly professional group of thieves were in and out in four minutes flat before the museum opened.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: The man behind Srebrenica: Ratko Mladic dies at 84
item.description: For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian War. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and of other war crimes. Now he has died in detention at The Hague.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Zambian opposition leader in police custody: state media
item.description: Zambia's national broadcaster reports that Brian Mundubile, who wanted to challenge this month's presidential election results, and his running mate have surrendered to police and are being interviewed.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Nepal flooding: 'We are disconnected from Kathmandu'
item.description: DW spoke with people from the Nepali regions devastated by flash floods about the fates of their family members, with a government minister warning that the state was not ready for a disaster of such magnitude.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ex-Bosnian Serb military leader Ratko Mladic dead at 84
item.description: The former Bosnian Serb general was convicted of genocide committed during the bloody 1992-95 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Could new US sanctions tear China and Iran apart?
item.description: Washington's strategy of putting maximum economic pressure on Iran is tempered by its desire to smooth political tensions with China.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: What does Saxony-Anhalt's election mean for migrants?
item.description: The AfD could make history in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt. For many people with a migration background, the September 6 state election raises questions about belonging, security and their future in Germany.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: DW users on life in Russia: 'People are mad as hell'
item.description: Official polling suggests public sentiment in Russia is deteriorating as economic pressure builds. DW asked its users to share their experiences.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: CDU's Volkmann: Ukraine aid is not charity
item.description: Former German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's grandson Johannes Volkmann spoke to DW about why Germany must continue to support Ukraine.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Meta settles in US states lawsuit on teen user addiction
item.description: Meta has agreed to pay what could amount to billions of dollars and to implement platform usage limitations on young users in a lawsuit brought by US states. The challenge revolved around addiction issues and overuse.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Could Syria become the focus of an Israeli-Turkish conflict?
item.description: An Israeli attack on a Syrian military airfield just recently demonstrated once again that Syria is becoming a key battleground for the rivalry between regional powers. At the forefront: Israel and Turkey.
